title: Playing with Clem: the band, style and tonguing
summary: Barnes joins Clem's band, whose leader he compares to Kid Thomas, and the group discusses tonguing in trumpet playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: No, this band.
Well this is the next band you were to?
Yeah, next band.
Well who was in this band?
I played with Umarish and I remember who was in this band. It's been so long. Oh sure man.
It's hard. Just lucky to know.
Didn't he have some brothers or something that played music?
Clem? Clem? Yeah. But I played with Clem and I played with Riley. Which Riley?
Amos Riley. Theodore Riley's daddy in other words.
Amos Riley. Who?
Theodore Riley. You know the young trumpet player? Yeah.
He's an ordinary young fella. I don't guess you ever played with him. He's pretty good.
Yeah. Yeah.
Well I played with his daddy but I don't know, never knows none of his sons, they'd watch some of me.

No. Now was he the leader of the band? Yeah. This Edwauke Clem? Yeah. He was the leader of the band. What kind of style did he play? Can you think of anybody that we heard that he played like? Let's see who. I don't remember now. Well like Kid Thomas?

Well partly like Thomas. Yeah partly like Thomas. How about Charlie Love? But he had a, a, a tongue in his thing. You know like cutting over. Uh huh. See a, see a cutting over the tongue like that. Did he play anything like Charlie Love? No. I think it's more like Thomas.
Did he have any feature number?
No. No feature number.
No.
Good blues man? He was the blues man too. Most of all of us sons played blues in the future house.
Was he, what you call a straight man or a musician? A pretty straight man. He didn't, would he get off ever?
Well I'm sure.
About a sudden he'd get off. Well what is this ta-ta trumpet playing? What does that mean?
That means a man cut off his tongue. Ta-ta-ta-ta? Striking, striking.
Yeah.

You hear, right now you hear some musician cut off. He strikes, you know his tongue is striped. Other musicians are blowing out. But you catch the medicine they strike. They can notice that noise when you go up to night. They see the strike. They might not know they're doing it but they do it. Now you had a little band with Clem, was that about six pieces?
